balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For LKQ Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For LKQ Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For LKQ Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For LKQ Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For LKQ Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For LKQ Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For LKQ Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For LKQ Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Revenue split across LKQ's reporting segments: North America wholesale salvage/aftermarket parts, Europe wholesale distribution (Sator/Rhiag/Elit, ~18 countries) and Specialty (RV/towing/performance accessories, under an active sale process).

For LKQ Corporation: Europe is roughly a third of revenue and is the segment in crisis -- a German ERP migration plus UK/Benelux volume declines drove organic revenue down 9.8% in Q3 2026. North America (about half of revenue) has stayed comparatively stable, which is why a consolidated revenue chart alone hides the story.

What to watch:

  • Europe's revenue trend relative to North America's
  • Self Service is excluded -- divested to Pacific Avenue Capital Partners in October 2025

segmentEbitdaMargin.title: Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin
segmentEbitdaMargin.content:
Each segment's adjusted EBITDA divided by its own revenue -- the cleanest cross-segment profitability comparison, independent of each segment's size.

For LKQ Corporation: Europe's margin collapsed from roughly 10% to roughly 4-5% through 2026 as the ERP disruption and volume declines hit, while North America's margin has held up. Q3 2026 also carried $111m of non-cash impairments ($88m Specialty goodwill, $23m Romania net assets held for sale) that sit below segment EBITDA but drove the quarter to a net loss.

What to watch:

  • Whether Europe's margin stabilises or keeps deteriorating next quarter
  • The gap to North America's margin as a read on execution, not just macro

organicGrowth.title: Organic revenue growth
organicGrowth.content:
Company-reported revenue growth excluding currency translation and the effect of acquisitions/divestitures -- the cleanest read on underlying volume and pricing.

For LKQ Corporation: organic growth has been negative every quarter shown and worsened to -5.4% in Q3 2026, driven almost entirely by Europe's operational breakdown; this is the metric management, the board and the activist pressure behind the January 2026 strategic review are all focused on.

What to watch:

  • Sign and trend, not the absolute level -- consecutive negative quarters signal a structural problem, not just a weak repairable-claims environment
  • Whether the rate of decline is stabilising once the ERP migration is behind Europe

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For LKQ Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For LKQ Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
